blindness.agent_reported_external_sources:
No web search, no standout source, no other repositories. I did not read the
downloaded standout crate sources at any point. General Rust and clap 4
knowledge, yes — the clap derive surface, `ArgMatches::ids()` /
`try_get_one`, `std::io::IsTerminal`, `Vec::split_off`.

Two facts I needed are not in docs/, and I obtained them from the toolchain and
the running binary rather than from any source or external reference. Both are
load-bearing, so flagging them plainly:

- The argument id standout injects for `--answers` is
  `_standout_questionnaire_answers` (and `_standout_questionnaire_yes` for
  `--yes`). I found this by printing `ArgMatches::ids()` from inside my own
  hook at runtime. Because that spelling is a framework-internal id and not
  documented, I did not hard-code it: `require_answer_source` matches any
  supplied id containing "answers".
- `CommandContext::input_sources()` returns `&InputSources`, whose `.stdin()`
  returns `&dyn StdinReader` carrying `is_terminal()`. I found the shape by
  deliberately assigning the call to `()` and reading the compiler's
  mismatched-types error. docs/topics/testing.md documents that `StdinReader`
  is the seam, but not how to reach it from a hook.

Also empirical rather than documented: the exact confirmation-prompt behaviour
of standout's own gate. I never observed it, because this environment cannot
allocate a pty (see friction), so I took the gate over rather than trust it.

answers.docs.gaps:
1. The documented confirmation gate does not match what SPEC.md requires, and
   this is the one substantive divergence in the build.
   docs/guides/derived-questionnaires.md: "Questionnaire commands get `--yes`
   from the framework. Without it, Standout asks for an exact `yes` on an
   attended controlling terminal after any configured review."
   SPEC.md: "reads one answer line: `yes` or `y` (case-insensitive) confirms".
   An exact `yes` cannot accept `y`, `Y` or `YES`. There is no documented way to
   supply a different confirmation predicate — `CommandConfig` offers
   `questionnaire::<T>()`, `questionnaire_with_form::<T, _>(form)` and
   `questionnaire_with_form_and_review::<T, _, _>(form, review)`, and review
   runs *before* the gate rather than replacing it. So I took the gate over; see
   the workarounds answer.
   Caveat on my own claim: I could not observe standout's gate directly (no pty
   here), so "exact `yes`" is the doc's word, not something I reproduced.

2. Two words in the same sentence disagree about which terminal the gate reads.
   Same page: "an exact `yes` on an attended controlling terminal", then "Piped
   stdin never confirms a run". A controlling terminal is reachable via /dev/tty
   even when stdin is a pipe, so those two are only consistent if the gate
   actually keys off stdin. SPEC.md is unambiguous ("Piped stdin never
   confirms"), so my gate keys off the stdin seam.

3. The framework-injected argument ids are undocumented.
   docs/guides/derived-questionnaires.md shows the user-facing spelling
   (`myapp import --answers answers.txt`) but nothing tells a hook author what
   to call `matches.get_one(...)` with. The real id is
   `_standout_questionnaire_answers`. A hook that wants to know whether
   `--answers` was supplied — exactly what SPEC.md's bounded-failure rule needs
   — has to discover this at runtime.

4. Reaching the stdin seam from a hook is undocumented.
   docs/topics/testing.md says stdin "lives on the `InputSources` value for that
   run" and docs/crates/input/topics/framework-integration.md shows
   `ctx.input_sources()` being passed *into* `resolve_from`, but nothing shows
   reading a fact off it. `ctx.input_sources().stdin().is_terminal()` is what
   works, and it matters: a hook that calls `std::io::stdin().is_terminal()`
   instead silently ignores `TestHarness::interactive_stdin()`. That is exactly
   the pitfall docs/guides/intro-to-testing.md warns about for handlers
   ("Handlers that bypass `standout-input`"), but the fix it implies —
   `StdinSource::new()` / `read_if_piped()` — consumes stdin, which a guard hook
   must not do.

5. Hook ordering under `#[derive(Dispatch)]` is unspecified.
   docs/topics/app-configuration.md documents ordering for `CommandConfig` and
   even notes "Stating a single ordering rule for pre-dispatch hooks ... is
   issue #352". docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md documents the equivalent
   variant attributes with no ordering statement at all. The derive's attribute
   order does not control it (friction 1).

6. docs/guides/minimal-single-crate.md's `#[handler]` example does not compile
   as written (friction 4), and docs/guides/intro-to-testing.md's `serial`
   import instruction is incomplete (friction 3).
answers.friction:
1. Hook ordering is not controllable through the `#[derive(Dispatch)]`
   attributes. docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md lists both `questionnaire =
   <path>` and `pre_dispatch = <path>` as variant attributes, and says "Several
   `#[dispatch(…)]` attributes may sit on one variant; they merge before
   anything reads them." I wrote
   `#[dispatch(pure, pre_dispatch = require_answer_source, questionnaire =
   ProvisionAnswers, template_name = "provision")]`
   expecting the written order to hold. It did not: `formlike provision` still
   failed with
   `Hook error: hook error (pre-dispatch): questionnaire input `questionnaire`:
   No input provided and no default available.`
   — the questionnaire's message, so my guard never ran. Switching to the
   `CommandConfig` form from docs/topics/app-configuration.md
   (`.pre_dispatch(require_answer_source).questionnaire::<ProvisionAnswers>()
   .pre_dispatch(confirm_provisioning)`) gave the documented ordering and
   worked first try. That cost the `Dispatch` derive: I now register the one
   command with `App::builder().command_with(...)`.

2. The questionnaire's own no-input diagnostic is not actionable. For
   `formlike provision` with stdin not a terminal, all the user gets is
   `No input provided and no default available.`
   SPEC.md requires "a stderr message naming what was missing and how to supply
   it (the offending question id, or the `--answers`/`--yes` flag that would
   have unblocked the run)". This message names neither, which is the whole
   reason `require_answer_source` exists.

3. `use standout_test::serial;` is not sufficient on its own.
   docs/guides/intro-to-testing.md says "The `serial_test::serial` attribute is
   re-exported from `standout_test` for convenience: `use standout_test::serial;`".
   Doing exactly that fails to compile, once per annotated test:
   `error[E0433]: cannot find module or crate `serial_test``
   `  = help: if you wanted to use a crate named `serial_test`, use `cargo add serial_test``
   The re-exported macro expands to a `serial_test::` path, so `serial_test`
   has to be a direct dev-dependency too. Added `serial_test = "3"`.

4. `#[handler]` requires the view type to be public, which the docs' own
   examples do not show. `docs/guides/minimal-single-crate.md` declares
   `#[derive(Serialize)] struct TodoResult` (private) alongside a `#[handler]`.
   Copying that shape gave
   `error[E0446]: private type `ProvisionView` in public interface`
   `  67 |     #[handler]  ^^^^^^^^^^ can't leak private type`
   Making the struct `pub` fixes it; the doc example as written would not
   compile.

5. `TestResult::stdout()` has no trailing newline, but the binary's stdout does.
   `result.assert_stdout_eq("provisioned mysite in us (public: yes)\n")` fails
   with a diff whose two halves are visually identical:
   `--- expected --- provisioned mysite in us (public: yes)`
   `--- actual ----- provisioned mysite in us (public: yes)`
   The harness captures before the final write that adds the newline (`od -c` on
   the real binary confirms the process does emit a trailing `\n`). Not wrong,
   but the identical-looking diff cost time.

6. Environment, not standout: this sandbox cannot allocate a pty, so I could not
   drive the attended-terminal paths against a real terminal.
   `script: openpty: Operation not permitted`, and Python's `pty.fork()` gives
   `OSError: out of pty devices` even with the sandbox disabled. Interactive
   collection is therefore covered through `TestHarness::prompts(...)` and the
   `ScriptedResponder` seam instead; the confirmation prompt's own line reading
   is not covered by any test.

answers.summary:
`formlike` as specified in SPEC.md, complete and building clean (`cargo build`
emits no code warnings; the only warning is this sandbox's `xcrun` noise).

It is built on standout's derived-questionnaire path. A `ProvisionAnswers`
struct deriving `standout::Questionnaire` declares the three questions; the
field names are the stable ids (name, region, public). `region` is a
`QuestionnaireChoices` enum over eu/us defaulting to eu, `public` is a bool
defaulting to no, `name` is required and carries a field validator restricting
it to lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. The questionnaire is attached with
`CommandConfig::questionnaire::<ProvisionAnswers>()`, so standout supplies the
`provision questions` subcommand, `--answers FILE`, `--answers -` and `--yes`.
The handler reads `ctx.questionnaire()?` and renders one line from
`src/templates/provision.jinja`.

Two application-owned pre-dispatch hooks sit around the questionnaire:
- `require_answer_source` runs before it. When no `--answers` was given and
  stdin is not an attended terminal, it fails with a message naming the three
  question ids and the `--answers` spellings that would unblock the run.
  Without it the questionnaire's own diagnostic is the bare "No input provided
  and no default available.", which names neither a question nor a flag.
- `confirm_provisioning` runs after it, and is the confirmation gate.

Verified by running the binary: `provision questions` prints the sheet (exit 0);
a completed sheet from a file or from `--answers -` with `--yes` prints exactly
`provisioned <name> in <region> (public: <yes|no>)` on stdout, exit 0, with zero
bytes on stderr; blank answers take the declared defaults; a missing or
ill-formed answer fails with exit 1, empty stdout and a stderr diagnostic naming
the offending question id; a missing `--answers` or a needed-but-impossible
confirmation fails with exit 1 promptly (checked against a pipe held open for 30
seconds — it does not wait); unknown commands and flags exit 2.

There are also 19 in-process tests in `src/main.rs` (`cargo test`, all passing)
using `standout-test`'s `TestHarness`, including the interactive-collection
paths driven through the `ScriptedResponder` prompt seam.
answers.workarounds:
1. `take_over_confirmation` in src/main.rs rewrites argv. Because standout's
   confirmation gate accepts only `yes` and SPEC.md also requires `y`, every
   real provisioning run is handed `--yes` before it reaches the framework —
   which stands the framework's gate down — and the application's own
   `confirm_provisioning` hook asks the question instead. The function returns a
   `ConfirmGate { required }` recording whether the *user* actually asked to
   skip confirming, which is what the hook keys off; it goes in via
   `.app_state(gate)`.
   It deliberately does not rewrite `provision questions` (which rejects
   `--yes`: `formlike provision questions --yes` exits 2), nor any `--help` /
   `-h` / `--version` / `-V` line.
   Flag placement is a heuristic. The flag is appended, because clap echoes the
   arguments it already accepted in a parse error's usage line and a flag
   wedged in front of a typo makes that line read as though `--yes` were
   required. The exception is a line whose last token starts with `-`, is longer
   than one character and has no `=` — an option that may still want its value —
   where the flag goes in front of that token instead, so `formlike provision
   --answers` stays the exit-2 usage error it should be rather than reading
   `--yes` as the filename.
   Known cosmetic cost: `formlike provision --nope` reports
   `error: unexpected argument '--nope' found` (correct, exit 2) but with
   `Usage: formlike provision --yes` beneath it, because `--nope` trips the
   last-token heuristic and the injected flag lands in front of it. The
   heuristic cannot tell an unknown flag from an option awaiting a value without
   the schema, and I chose the correct exit code over the tidier usage line.

2. `require_answer_source` detects `--answers` by matching any supplied
   argument id containing "answers" rather than naming
   `_standout_questionnaire_answers`, since that id is framework-internal and
   undocumented. Matching by shape is deliberate: it is loose, but it will not
   break the way a hard-coded private id would.

3. Not a workaround so much as a consequence: registering the command through
   `App::builder().command_with(...)` rather than `#[derive(Dispatch)]` is what
   buys the hook ordering the design needs. `Commands` still derives clap's
   `Subcommand`; it no longer derives `Dispatch`.
